title: Why your power bill went up (a building you've never seen)
description:
On PJM, the grid that serves 67 million people in 13 states and Washington, D.C., the yearly auction that pays power plants to stand ready went from $28.92 to $333.44 per megawatt-day in three auctions. The grid's market monitor estimates data centers caused 63% of the first jump.

Sources:
- DOE Releases New Report Evaluating Increase in Electricity Demand from Data Centers (LBNL 2024 report) — U.S. Department of Energy: https://www.energy.gov/articles/doe-releases-new-report-evaluating-increase-electricity-demand-data-centers
- PJM Auction Procures 134,479 MW of Generation Resources (17 Dec 2025) — PJM Interconnection: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2025-releases/20251217-pjm-auction-procures-134479-mw-of-generation-resources.pdf
- 2024/2025 Base Residual Auction Report — PJM Interconnection: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/markets-ops/rpm/rpm-auction-info/2024-2025/2024-2025-base-residual-auction-report.ashx
- 2025/2026 Base Residual Auction Report — PJM Interconnection: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/markets-ops/rpm/rpm-auction-info/2025-2026/2025-2026-base-residual-auction-report.ashx
- 2027/2028 Base Residual Auction Report — PJM Interconnection: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/markets-ops/rpm/rpm-auction-info/2027-2028/2027-2028-bra-report.pdf
- Projected data center growth spurs PJM capacity prices by factor of 10 — IEEFA (Cathy Kunkel): https://ieefa.org/resources/projected-data-center-growth-spurs-pjm-capacity-prices-factor-10
- Data center power demands again drive record power auction prices (17 Dec 2025) — Maryland Office of People's Counsel: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MDOPC/bulletins/4006939

Labels: the 2028 share (6.7-12%) is LBNL's estimate for the Department of Energy; the 63% and $9.3 billion are the market monitor's estimate (Monitoring Analytics, via IEEFA); the D.C. bill figures (+$21 a month, about $10 of it from the auction) are Pepco residential averages from June 2025, with the half estimated by D.C.'s consumer counsel (via IEEFA). Prices are the PJM-wide (rest of RTO) clearing prices; some zones paid more. $529.80 is PJM's own no-cap simulation for 2027/28.
